apps.title: Vet Study 2.0
apps.description: A veterinary e-learning companion for keeping revision material close when you are away from your desk.
apps.workflow: Pick one syllabus topic before opening the app. After reading, close it and explain the key points aloud; check gaps against your course outline.
apps.access: Free to install · contains ads. Content availability may change.
apps.bestFit: A quick revision companion between classes. Pair any summary with the unit in your university outline.
apps.limits: Your syllabus remains the checklist for what you must cover. App content can vary by topic and update.

apps.title: VetConnect
apps.description: A veterinary drug index for looking up drug and brand information in an Indian practice context.
apps.workflow: Use it to connect a generic drug to its class and indications. Cross-check species, formulation and current product information with your clinical supervisor.
apps.access: Free to install · contains ads. The listing describes offline and online use.
apps.bestFit: Connect a brand name with the generic medicine and its pharmacological class when revising.
apps.limits: A name match is not a treatment decision. Check species, concentration, route and the current product label.

apps.title: MSD Vet Manual
apps.description: A broad veterinary reference for reviewing diseases, diagnostic approaches and clinical background across species.
apps.workflow: Start with a condition from rounds. Read its overview and diagnostic approach, then write a short problem list before discussing the case.
apps.access: Free reference. Download the core content first; some media and features need an internet connection.
apps.bestFit: Read the background to a clinical problem: causes, examination findings and how diagnoses are distinguished.
apps.limits: Separate a broad overview from the patient-specific decision. Check species and article references with your supervisor.

apps.title: IVRI Veterinary Clinical Care
apps.description: An Indian field-practice learning aid covering common medicine, gynaecology and surgery presentations.
apps.workflow: Before a supervised field visit, review one common presentation such as bloat or dystocia. Compare the history, examination and differential diagnoses with what you observe.
apps.access: Free to install. Developed by ICAR-IVRI and IASRI; includes clinical explanations and educational procedure videos.
apps.bestFit: Prepare for livestock case discussions and connect a presentation with the history and examination you need.
apps.limits: Educational procedure material does not replace supervised skills training or local clinical protocols.

apps.title: 3D Dog Anatomy
apps.description: Explore canine skeletal, muscular and internal anatomy from multiple angles.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

apps.title: 3D Cat Anatomy
apps.description: Use a feline model to compare spatial relationships with canine anatomy.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

apps.title: 3D Horse Anatomy
apps.description: Rotate an equine model and isolate systems to understand structures in three dimensions.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

apps.description: View porcine internal systems layer by layer and practise identifying landmarks.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

apps.description: Explore caprine systems and highlight structures for comparative anatomy revision.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

apps.title: 3D Bird Anatomy
apps.description: Study a pigeon model for avian bones, muscles and internal organs.
apps.workflow: Hide one system, name the exposed structures, then reveal it to check yourself. Pair the model with your dissection or osteology notes.
apps.access: Paid publisher app · Telegram collection link pending.

resources.title: VetBVSc — year-wise notes
resources.description: BVSc subject and year collections, including links to TANUVAS material.
resources.use: Finding a second explanation or a subject collection. Check older course codes against your own outline.
resources.access: Public pages; linked files have their own access settings.
resources.start: Start from your year, then the subject. Match each unit heading to your current outline before collecting PDFs.
resources.takeaway: Write down the unit title, source and any missing topics. Avoid treating an old course code as proof that the syllabus matches.

resources.title: Vetscraft — subject explanations
resources.description: Readable veterinary topic explanations across basic, production and clinical subjects.
resources.use: Understanding a difficult concept before returning to your textbook.
resources.access: Public articles; individual courses may have different access terms.
resources.start: Start with the subject and unit you are studying. Compare the resource’s headings with your university outline.
resources.takeaway: Record the author, date and source. Check any missing topic against your recommended text rather than assuming the collection is complete.

resources.title: Vets Duo — subject lecture notes
resources.description: Subject-based BVSc collections covering basic sciences, animal production and clinical study.
resources.use: Comparing lecture notes and locating TANUVAS-labelled collections.
resources.access: Public directory; availability depends on each linked collection.
resources.start: Start with the subject and unit you are studying. Compare the resource’s headings with your university outline.
resources.takeaway: Record the author, date and source. Check any missing topic against your recommended text rather than assuming the collection is complete.

resources.title: DrVet — veterinary study archive
resources.description: An archive of subject notes, exam material and veterinary study posts.
resources.use: Looking for older revision posts or question-paper references. Verify the year and original source.
resources.access: Public posts; external files may require separate access.
resources.start: Start with the subject and unit you are studying. Compare the resource’s headings with your university outline.
resources.takeaway: Record the author, date and source. Check any missing topic against your recommended text rather than assuming the collection is complete.

resources.title: GreatVets — BVSc revision
resources.description: Veterinary notes organised for BVSc study and revision.
resources.use: Getting a concise topic overview. Check any generated explanation against a textbook.
resources.access: Public notes; other features may require an account.
resources.start: Use a short explanation to identify what you do not understand, then read the matching textbook section.
resources.takeaway: Check diagrams, species differences and any AI-generated explanation against a credited source.

resources.title: MSD Veterinary Manual
resources.description: Veterinary disease overviews, diagnostic background, tables and clinical learning material.
resources.use: Reading around a case after rounds; start with the species and clinical problem.
resources.access: Free web reference. Educational use does not replace clinical supervision.
resources.start: Start with the species and presenting problem. Read the diagnostic approach before jumping to a treatment section.
resources.takeaway: Make a problem list and list the evidence needed to distinguish the possibilities; discuss the case under supervision.

resources.title: eClinPath — Cornell clinical pathology
resources.description: An online clinical pathology textbook covering interpretation of haematology, chemistry and other laboratory findings.
resources.use: Understanding why a result changes, rather than memorising a reference interval alone.
resources.access: Free educational text; interpret results with the reporting laboratory’s intervals.
resources.start: Choose the laboratory test or cell finding you need to understand. Read sample quality and interpretation alongside the result.
resources.takeaway: Use the reporting laboratory’s reference interval and consider pre-analytical factors; a number alone is not a diagnosis.

resources.title: IVIS — veterinary reading & continuing education
resources.description: Veterinary proceedings, publications and learning resources from an international education network.
resources.use: Reading more deeply about a clinical question or preparing a seminar.
resources.access: Free registration may be required; access varies by item.
resources.start: Search a focused species-and-topic question. Check whether the item is a review, a conference proceeding or other learning material.
resources.takeaway: Record publication year and references; use the original study when a specific claim matters.

resources.title: PubMed — find the original paper
resources.description: A biomedical literature search service that includes veterinary and comparative research.
resources.use: Finding a primary study. Add species and study design to your search; read methods before trusting a conclusion.
resources.access: Free search and abstracts; full-text availability depends on the publisher.
resources.start: Build a question from species, problem, intervention or exposure, and outcome. Try synonyms if the first search is too narrow.
resources.takeaway: Read the study population, design and limitations. An abstract or a statistically significant result is not enough to establish clinical usefulness.

resources.title: WOAH — animal health codes & manuals
resources.description: International standards and manuals for animal health, diagnostic testing, welfare and veterinary public health.
resources.use: Looking up the official context for disease control, surveillance or diagnostic standards.
resources.access: Public standards; use the current edition and relevant chapter.
resources.start: Choose the relevant code or manual and locate the disease or standard by name. Check the edition and chapter.
resources.takeaway: Distinguish international guidance from the rules implemented by the relevant Indian authority or institution.

resources.title: VCI — veterinary education & registration rules
resources.description: The official collection of veterinary legislation, registration regulations and education standards.
resources.use: Checking the source behind a curriculum or registration claim.
resources.access: Public regulations; use your university’s current implementation as well.
resources.start: Find the regulation or educational standard behind the question, then read the relevant clause and amendments.
resources.takeaway: Match the document date to the rule you need; your university’s current notices explain local implementation.

resources.title: IVRI — postgraduate study information
resources.description: Official information about master’s study and veterinary disciplines at IVRI.
resources.use: Shortlisting postgraduate subjects and checking the institution’s current admission route.
resources.access: Public information; the current admission notice determines eligibility and dates.
resources.start: Choose the programme and discipline, then locate the current admission notice and its selection process.
resources.takeaway: Track exam registration, institutional application and counselling separately where required. Check deadlines in the official notice.

careerSources.note: Read the current examination bulletin and the separate admission/counselling notice for the relevant veterinary programme.

careers.title: Pet clinics & hospitals
careers.summary: Examine pets, explain problems and follow their recovery.
careers.work: Examine patients, plan tests and treatment, keep records and explain home care. Emergency and specialist roles need additional skills.
careers.entry: Complete BVSc & AH, the required internship and applicable registration. Look for a role with a named mentor; an MVSc is not required for every general-practice job.
careers.fit: You enjoy hands-on care and helping worried pet owners.
careers.first: Observe a full clinic shift with permission. Ask how a new graduate gets help with a difficult case.
careers.watch: Who supervises you? What are the night duties, case load and referral arrangements?

careers.title: Livestock & dairy practice
careers.summary: Solve farm problems, from one sick animal to a whole herd.
careers.work: Support reproduction, udder health, disease prevention and farm management. Use herd records as well as individual examinations.
careers.entry: Clinical roles need BVSc & AH and applicable registration. Employers may also ask for field experience or relevant postgraduate training.
careers.fit: You like farms, field visits and practical problem-solving.
careers.first: Join supervised farm rounds. Follow one herd problem from history-taking to a practical prevention plan.
careers.watch: Check travel, emergency cover, biosecurity and whether you will have experienced support.

careers.title: Poultry, feed & production
careers.summary: Keep flocks healthy and spot problems in production data.
careers.work: Work in flock health, biosecurity, hatcheries, feed or technical support. Some posts focus on operations rather than clinical care.
careers.entry: Check the employer’s requirements. Production experience or a relevant MVSc may help for specialist roles; clinical duties carry registration requirements.
careers.fit: You enjoy prevention, numbers and improving how a farm works.
careers.first: Visit a unit through your college. Learn its biosecurity routine and one key production measure.
careers.watch: Is this a health, operations or sales role? Ask about travel, targets and farm residency.

careers.title: Government veterinary services
careers.summary: Deliver field care and animal-health programmes for communities.
careers.work: Depending on the post: dispensary work, vaccination, disease surveillance, extension or administration.
careers.entry: Use the exact PSC, department or UPSC notice. Degree, registration, age, language and experience rules vary. Some posts are for deputation, not fresh graduates.
careers.fit: You want public service, rural outreach and organised programmes.
careers.first: Read one current official vacancy. Make a checklist of eligibility, exam topics, documents and deadlines.
careers.watch: There is no single exam for every veterinary officer post. Follow the recruiting authority’s notice.

careers.title: Armed forces · Army RVC
careers.summary: Veterinary care and officer responsibilities in the Indian Army.
careers.fit: You want veterinary work within military service and can accept postings, training and service discipline.
careers.work: The Remount Veterinary Corps supports Army animals, including equines and dogs, with care, disease prevention, management and related public-health responsibilities. Duties vary by appointment.
careers.entry: Follow the current Army RVC Short Service Commission notice. Recognised veterinary qualifications and registration are central; the notice sets age, category, medical and other conditions. Past notices used shortlisting, SSB assessment, medical examination and merit-based selection.
careers.first: Read a current or archived RVC officer notice, separate its permanent requirements from cycle-specific dates, and speak to a serving or former RVC officer about duties and postings.
careers.watch: This is an officer career, not simply a clinic job in uniform. Verify service terms, medical standards and posting expectations. Veterinary nursing-assistant recruitment is a different entry route.

careers.title: Public health & One Health
careers.summary: Connect animal health, human health and the environment.
careers.work: Possible work includes zoonoses, food hygiene, epidemiology, surveillance and public-health projects.
careers.entry: Check each vacancy’s accepted qualifications. A relevant MVSc, MPH or epidemiology course may help for some roles, but does not create automatic eligibility.
careers.fit: You like outbreaks, population-level questions and working with other disciplines.
careers.first: Write a one-page brief on a zoonosis: who is at risk, what the evidence says and one practical prevention step.
careers.watch: Before paying for another course, check whether real jobs you want recognise it.

careers.title: Diagnostics & laboratories
careers.summary: Turn a sample into an answer a clinical team can use.
careers.work: Handle samples, run tests, check quality and help interpret findings. Clinical diagnostic and research laboratories have different roles.
careers.entry: Start with supervised laboratory experience. Specialist, research and leadership posts may need relevant postgraduate qualifications or experience.
careers.fit: You enjoy careful methods, microscopy and asking what a result really means.
careers.first: Follow one sample from collection to the final report in your teaching laboratory.
careers.watch: Ask about quality control, sample safety and supervision. A positive result alone is not a complete diagnosis.

careers.title: Teaching & research
careers.summary: Investigate questions and help the next batch understand them.
careers.work: Teach, research, supervise and publish. Project roles can be temporary and depend on grant funding.
careers.entry: Relevant MVSc and often PhD training support this route. NET, ARS and experience requirements depend on the specific post and current notice.
careers.fit: You enjoy explaining, reading critically and working through uncertain results.
careers.first: Join a supervised literature review or small project. Practise references, research ethics and basic statistics.
careers.watch: Compare the supervisor, funding and hands-on training—not just the degree or institute name.

careers.title: Animal-health industry
careers.summary: Work with medicines, vaccines, products and the people using them.
careers.work: Explore technical services, training, pharmacovigilance, regulatory support, product roles or sales. Daily work differs widely.
careers.entry: Read the actual job description. Some roles accept BVSc graduates; specialist and research posts may need MVSc, PhD or experience.
careers.fit: You like science, communication and working with business teams.
careers.first: Compare three genuine vacancies. Highlight repeated skills and make one work sample that demonstrates them.
careers.watch: Ask how success is measured: sales, training, scientific work or delivery. Check travel and targets.

careers.title: Wildlife, zoos & conservation
careers.summary: Support animal health alongside conservation and welfare teams.
careers.work: Help with preventive care, quarantine, diagnostics, rescue or rehabilitation. Openings can be limited or project-based.
careers.entry: Clinical work needs appropriate veterinary qualifications and registration. Relevant supervised experience or postgraduate study may be required.
careers.fit: You enjoy teamwork, population health and patient, careful fieldwork.
careers.first: Ask your college about a formal supervised placement. Learn safety and permit requirements before handling wildlife.
careers.watch: Check supervision, contract length and duties. Wildlife experience should never mean unsupervised capture or treatment.

careers.title: Shelters & animal welfare
careers.summary: Make good care possible for animals with limited resources.
careers.work: Support shelter health, sterilisation programmes, outbreak prevention, records and community education.
careers.entry: Clinical posts need BVSc & AH, applicable registration and supervised clinical competence. Management posts may ask for more experience.
careers.fit: You value community work and balancing individual care with population needs.
careers.first: Join a recognised supervised programme. Observe pain management, infection control and patient tracking.
careers.watch: Ask about facilities, caseload limits, mentorship and support for staff.

careers.title: Your own veterinary business
careers.summary: Build a clinic, service or product around a real need.
careers.work: Options include clinics, mobile care, farm consultancy, education or technology. Expect finance, operations and team management too.
careers.entry: Clinical ventures need relevant registration and local compliance. Permissions for premises, medicines, waste and business activity depend on the service and location.
careers.fit: You enjoy ownership, communication and solving both clinical and business problems.
careers.first: Talk to five potential users. Draft a simple plan for costs, supervision, equipment and referrals before investing.
careers.watch: Revenue is not profit. Include rent, staff, consumables, compliance and emergency costs.

careers.title: Writing, education & veterinary tech
careers.summary: Use veterinary knowledge to teach, explain or improve a product.
careers.work: Explore scientific writing, educational content, editing, product support or health-data projects. Some roles combine this with clinical work.
careers.entry: Build writing, teaching, data or product skills alongside your veterinary degree. Employers assess your work; clinical advice still carries professional responsibilities.
careers.fit: You like clear communication, checking evidence and making helpful resources.
careers.first: Make a small portfolio: a cited explainer, an evidence summary and a patient-education sheet. Remove identifying case details.
careers.watch: Check sources and avoid unsupported claims. A focused portfolio is more useful than calling yourself an expert.
